component.name: Apache Seata
component.description: Distributed transaction solution. The security model document is a SecretKey security announcement for Seata-Console, the user console shipped since 1.5.0 that offers query functionality for global transactions, branch transactions, and global lock information. Login uses a username/password verified by the backend, which issues a time-sensitive JWT token signed with a SecretKey; subsequent requests carry the JWT token, which the backend validates before returning data.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

threats.name: Data leakage or intrusion through default Seata-Console credentials and SecretKey
threats.description: Seata-Console's default configuration file contains default settings for the username, password, and SecretKey. Deploying to production without changing them risks data leakage or intrusion due to default credentials; users must change seata.console.user.username, seata.console.user.password, and seata.security.secretKey before the first deployment.

threats.name: Unnecessary public network access to Seata-Console
threats.description: Public network exposure of Seata-Console increases attack exposure. In a production environment, unnecessary public network access should be prohibited; even though Seata-Console does not store or display sensitive data, restricting access is strongly recommended.

controls.name: Username/password login with time-sensitive JWT tokens
controls.description: Seata-Console sends the username and password to the backend service for verification; on success the backend generates a time-sensitive JWT token based on a SecretKey. Subsequent visits carry the JWT token, which the backend validates, denying access if it is invalid.

controls.name: Change default username, password, and SecretKey before deployment
controls.description: When deploying Seata-Console for the first time, change the default username, password, and SecretKey (seata.console.user.username, seata.console.user.password, seata.security.secretKey in application.yml) before deployment. In a Kubernetes deployment, manage this information independently and hierarchically using ConfigMap/Secret resources.

controls.name: Prohibit unnecessary public network access
controls.description: In a production environment, prohibit unnecessary public network access to Seata-Console. If public network access is required, configure firewalls or ACL rules to restrict IP access.
